subject: Post-call: model fit & regression concerns / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@retailco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit & recommended next steps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning, Alex - great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side.

Recap
- Use case: automated product categorization and attribute extraction for RetailCo web catalog (high-precision mapping to 200+ category labels).
- Constraints: <200ms p95 latency preference for classification, privacy: PII redaction before logs, batch throughput ~2k reqs/min during peak.
- Current baseline: in-house rules + small ML model (precision ~0.94 on top-1 for recent sample).

Our recommendations (short list)
- Model candidates to evaluate:
  - llm-13b-int8 (Llama-3 13B int8) - good balance of quality/latency for classification prompts
  - mistral-7b-chat-quant - lower-cost fast option for embeddings+class prompts
  - redwood-curated-1 (sft ensemble) - highest quality, higher cost; use as gold eval target
- Quantization profile: int8 with KV cache enabled for longer context (helps recall on multi-attribute examples).
- Evaluation plan: we'll run a targeted eval on your prompt set (you'll find attached a starting prompt file) and share a short summary + examples.

Benchmarks & artifacts
- Attached: retailco_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + expected labels).
- We'll upload the eval reports and a short summary doc to the shared Drive link and update the HubSpot deal.

Immediate next steps
1) I'll kick off an eval run against the three candidate model variants using your prompt set. ETA: 24-48 hours.
2) Please confirm any additional edge cases or label mapping rules to include in the prompt set.
3) If you want, let's schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review results and decide on pin/rollout strategy.

If anything urgent comes up (e.g., procurement or security questions), loop in Dylan and Rishi - they're copied.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. Two quick clarifications before you run the eval:

- Can you share the benchmark template and the exact metrics you'll report? I care most about top-1 precision/recall for category mapping and a confusion breakdown for the top 20 labels.
- We've noticed some odd outputs in prod this week after a vendor model update (answers drifting on a couple of product categories). Is pinning/rollback something we can do quickly if we see regressions? What's the expected turnaround?

Also attaching a tiny sample (not the full feed) that surfaces the problematic cases - if you want to include them in the eval set.

Appreciate it - Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & recommended next steps

Great questions - answering inline and attaching initial evaluation artifacts.

Metrics we'll share
- Top-1 precision, Top-1 recall (macro + weighted), confusion matrix for top-20 labels, and per-label precision.
- Secondary metrics: token-efficiency (tokens/response), latency p50/p95, and failure mode sampling (examples where model returns ambiguous/missing label).

Links and artifacts
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-retailco-evals (I'll drop full reports here once the run completes).
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/RC-2027-042
- Attached summary: retailco_eval_summary_20270529.pdf (contains quick comparison: redwood-curated-1: top1 precision 0.96; llm-13b-int8: 0.93; mistral-7b-chat-quant: 0.90 on the sample prompt set). These are preliminary on the sample you shared.

About regressions / pinning
- Short answer: yes, you can pin to a specific model version or rollback a route. Options:
  - Pin at the inference config level to a specific model_version (we'll use model_version ids like mv-20270520-1).
  - Rollback route: if a new default produces a regression, we can rollback the route to the prior model_version in under an hour for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private installs turnaround depends on your deploy cadence but pinning is immediate.

If we see a quality regression in the evaluation run, propose this flow:
1) Hold traffic on the new variant and pin production to the last known-good model_version.
2) Rishi/infra will run a quick regression harness against the failing prompt set + a larger random sample.
3) If failures are confirmed, we can A/B test a patched variant or pin longer-term while engineering investigates.

I've attached the eval summary and the initial prompt set we ran. I'll follow up when the full run is complete with the per-label confusion matrices.

Thanks - I'll schedule the 30-min follow-up for next Tue and send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Looping in a quick technical note on regressions - copying the parts of Marissa's note for context.

Quoted: "If we see a quality regression in the evaluation run, propose this flow: 1) Hold traffic on the new variant and pin production to the last known-good model_version. 2) Rishi/infra will run a quick regression harness against the failing prompt set + a larger random sample."

What I'm seeing (internal):
- Yesterday our model owner pushed v1.3.0 for redwood-curated-1 which includes a tokenizer tweak and a small SFT refresh. On internal benchmarks this improved generation diversity but I'm seeing a measurable drop in strict label mapping precision for closed-vocab tasks (the category mapping case).
- Quick diff I ran: tokenization change altered how hyphenated SKUs and parenthetical qualifiers are tokenized which shifts logits for boundary tokens in classification prompts - that can manifest as label drift. I attached the regression diff (regression_diff.patch) with the tokenizer deltas and an example failing case.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) If RetailCo confirms the failing examples in the eval run, request permission to pin production to model_version:mv-20270520-1 (last known-good). Pinning is a config change and immediate for Hosted/Dedicated routes.
2) I'll run the regression harness (full ~5k sample) and post precise delta numbers (expected turnaround 3-4 hours once I have the full eval set).
3) If the harness confirms, we can either pin and plan a targeted SFT fix or run a constrained reroll of the SFT without the tokenization change.

Action items (internal)
- Marissa: confirm RetailCo is okay if we pin quickly in response to confirmed regression.
- Dylan: please prepare a canary config with pin to mv-20270520-1 so we can flip it with one API call if approved.
- Rishi: I'll run the harness once the full eval set is uploaded.

Thanks - I'll update this thread with harness numbers.

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
